title: Juniper and the Smile
premise: Folklorist Emrys Oyelaran arrives in the hollow of Juniper's Rest to record a harvest song the villagers will sing only once, never twice, and never in his presence. When an excavation crew unearths an iron door sealed from the inside, he realizes the song is not a celebration but a lock, renewed each year by every voice in the village — and his recording has taught the melody to something below. As the harvest moon rises, Emrys must learn the song's final verse from the village's last willing singer, a woman who remembers being buried behind that door as a child. In the end, Emrys sings the verse alone, trading his memory of home for the village's survival, and stays in Juniper's Rest as its newest keeper: belonging, at last, at the price of everything he was.
about_author: Jonah Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in remote coastal settlements before turning to fiction. They write horror about the quiet bargains communities make to keep existing.

chapters.title: The Song Sung Once
chapters.summary: Emrys Oyelaran, POV. Arriving in Juniper's Rest, Emrys records the harvest song from a distance, noting how villagers scatter when it ends and refuse to repeat it. His tape captures a second voice beneath the choir, faint and wrong. The emotional beat is unease disguised as professional curiosity — he tells himself documentation is harmless, even holy.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Alternating between Emrys and Maren, the excavation foreman. The crew breaches a hillside barrow and finds an iron door bolted shut from within; that night, everyone who touched it hums the song in their sleep. Emrys plays his recording and hears the buried voice answering back through his own speakers. The beat shifts from curiosity to dread: he has become part of the mechanism.

chapters.title: What the Verse Costs
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. He seeks out Odile, the eldest singer, who confesses she was sealed behind the door as a child and let out only by promising to teach the verse to whoever next learned the song. She begins teaching him, but each repetition erases one of his memories — first his mother's face, then his city, then why he came. The beat is grief accelerating toward sacrifice.

chapters.title: Harvest Moon Rising
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV, with Maren witnessing. On the night of the full moon, the door opens and the thing wearing the buried voice climbs toward the village singing his recording back at him. Emrys sings the final verse alone, unlearning himself line by line until the door closes on silence. Resolution: the village welcomes him warmly, a man with no past, finally belonging — and humming a song he'll never need to sing twice.
